title: Item Response Theory for AI Safety Benchmarks

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: applying IRT to safety benchmarks could make them more efficient and reliable, directly addressing the evaluation gap. The calibrated benchmark has independent intermediate value as a reusable tool.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: IRT is well-established with Python libraries (py-irt). Running models against benchmarks and fitting IRT models is intermediate-level statistics/ML work. Requires understanding both IRT theory and safety benchmarks.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Building an IRT-calibrated dataset requires running multiple models against a benchmark, fitting IRT parameters, and comparing ranking stability. Sustained effort with clear but multi-step deliverable.

novelty.reasoning: IRT for LLM evaluation is an active and rapidly maturing research area. Stanford's HELM framework already integrates IRT-based adaptive testing. 'Lost in Benchmarks? Rethinking LLM Benchmarking with IRT' (arXiv:2505.15055) directly applies IRT to rethink benchmarks. 'Learning Compact Representations of LLM Abilities via IRT' (arXiv:2510.00844) and AutoIRT (arXiv:2409.08823) provide automated calibration. Epoch AI has published an IRT-based Capability Index. PSN-IRT analysis across 11 benchmarks with 41,871 items is published. Applying IRT specifically to safety benchmarks is a minor application-domain extension of well-established methodology, not a novel contribution.
